This book covers AS topic 1 (business and its environment: 1.1–1.5) and the A Level external environment in topic 6.1. Cambridge Business is marked on four assessment objectives: knowledge (K), application (App) to the context, analysis (An) and evaluation (Ev). Our mark guides show where each type of mark comes from; calculations use M1 (method) and A1 (answer). Every calculation was checked by computer. The mark guides are our own and are not official Cambridge mark schemes.

Unit 1 of 10: Enterprise and Entrepreneurs

Key ideas

  • Business activity adds value by combining factors of production (land, labour, capital, enterprise) to satisfy needs and wants.
  • Added value = selling price − cost of bought-in materials.
  • Entrepreneur: someone who takes the risk of starting a business (qualities: innovation, risk-taking, determination, self-confidence, ability to raise finance).
  • Intrapreneur: an employee who acts like an entrepreneur inside an existing organisation (new products, processes).
  • Business plan: sets out objectives, market research, marketing plan, operations, finance (cash-flow forecast, break-even) — helps to obtain finance and to plan, but may be based on unreliable forecasts.
  • Social enterprise: has social or environmental objectives as well as financial ones (triple bottom line).
  • Role of enterprise in an economy: jobs, innovation, competition, economic growth, exports.

Worked examples

Example 1: a café sells a coffee for $4.00; the bought-in materials cost $1.20: added value = $2.80.

Example 2: an engineer in a car company develops a new battery design: intrapreneurship.

Example 3: a bank asks for a business plan before lending, to assess the risk.

10-mark exam-style question

Priya plans to open a bakery in a small town.

(a) Define the term "added value". [2]

(b) Explain two qualities Priya will need as an entrepreneur. [4]

(c) Analyse one benefit and one limitation of Priya writing a business plan. [4]

Answers and mark guide:

  • (a) The difference between the selling price of a product and the cost of the bought-in materials/components used to make it (K2; K1 for a partial answer).
  • (b) For each of two qualities, for example risk-taking (K1): Priya invests her savings in ovens and premises without knowing whether townspeople will buy her bread (App1); or determination, creativity, communication (K1 + App1 for each, max 4).
  • (c) Benefit: it helps her obtain a bank loan (K/App1) because the bank can see forecasts and judge her ability to repay (An1). Limitation: forecasts of sales may be inaccurate in a new market (K/App1), so decisions based on the plan could lead to cash-flow problems (An1).

Common mistakes

  1. Defining added value as profit.
  2. Listing qualities without linking them to the business in the case.
  3. Saying a business plan guarantees success.
  4. Confusing entrepreneurs with managers.
  5. Forgetting social enterprises have financial objectives too.

Quick recall

  1. Define entrepreneur.
  2. Define intrapreneur.
  3. Formula for added value?
  4. One purpose of a business plan?
  5. What is the triple bottom line?

Answers: 1) A person who takes the risk of starting and running a business. 2) An employee who develops new ideas within an existing business. 3) Selling price − cost of bought-in materials. 4) To obtain finance (or plan, set targets). 5) Profit, people (social) and planet (environmental) objectives.
